newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Sending a clear signal that the Chavalit government plans to get tough with protesters, top national security officials have resolved to adopt the "Malaysian way" of maintaining law and order. After a National Security Council meeting chaired by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, NSC secretary-general said that its participants "admire the peace and order" in neighbouring Malaysia. (THE NATION)

- The Constitution Scrutiny Committee has decided to fix the number of MPs on a party list at 100 and from electoral constituencies at 400 persons. The members, discussing the make-up of the new Parliament, also agree to reject a proposal calling for the new constitution to clearly stipulate that those on the party list be nominees for cabinet seats. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Regulators are set to revoke the licences of troubled finance companies, allow market forces to cause them to go under and restrict their business to going after money owed to them, Bank of Thailand (BOT) officials say. At the heart of the mergers and acquisitions package, to which authorities are now applying the finishing touches, lies a purchase and assumption method. (THE NATION)

- Bangchak Petroleum (BP) is preparing to seek investment privileges from the Board of Investment (BOI) for its 1.5 billion baht project to produce cleaner diesel. BP senior executive vice-president says the operation to reduce sulfur content in diesel is in line with government policy. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Union Bank shareholders have agreed to end a six-year corporate fight and to boost the bank's registered capital by 800 million baht. Union Bank's current registered capital of 800 million baht, 750 million of which is paid-up, is the lowest among the country's 15 banks. (BANGKOK POST)
